nearbyCountiesFullText.nwsHeadline: AIR QUALITY ALERT IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 AM EST THIS MORNING
nearbyCountiesFullText.description:
The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory for Elkhart county, IN in
effect utnil 10 AM EDT this morning.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM 2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors
closed as much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/

000
FXUS63 KIWX 170816
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
316 AM EST Tue Nov 17 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Some patchy shallow fog is possible this morning. Localized visibilities
  of less than one half mile are possible, but coverage should 
  be much more limited in comparison to Monday morning.

- A moderating temperature trend this week. The warmest days are 
  Thursday through Saturday with highs in the low to mid 60s.

- Dry conditions are expected this week with some rain chances 
  returning Saturday night into Sunday morning.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 310 AM EST Tue Nov 17 2026

A low level ridge axis continues to slowly migrate east this 
morning. Boundary layer decoupling and maintenance of weak low level 
flow has been sufficient for some vsby restrictions in fog 
especially from west central Indiana into far northeast 
Indiana/northwest Ohio. Near term RAP/HRRR progs suggest 
greatest potential for patchy dense fog early this morning 
roughly for southeast half of the area where low level flow will
remain a bit weaker.

After early morning fog dissipates. pleasant conditions are expected 
today with little in the way of thermal advection over the past 24 
hours. With another day of similar full insolation, a 
persistence forecast from yesterday was utilized as a first 
guess max temp forecast for today with highs in the 50 to 55 
degree range.

Quiet weather continues today/tonight with fog potential once 
again the main concern tonight. Current thinking is that this 
will continue to be a progressively lesser concern in comparison
to the past few nights as low level flow will be a bit stronger
with slight eastward progression of the low level ridge axis. 
If patchy shallow fog does develop again, would suspect that 
far northeast Indiana into northwest Ohio would be more 
favorable but forecast confidence is too low to include at this 
time.

Will be monitoring the progression of an upper level trough across 
the Pac NW into California this morning as it lifts northeast to the 
Upper MS Valley by early Thursday. Low level height gradient will 
strengthen downstream of this feature with sfc winds expected to 
increase a bit each day for Wednesday and Thursday. Mixing heights 
in warm advection will be limited however, which should cap
gusts to the 20 to 25 mph range Wed/Thu. No significant changes
were made to inherited max temps which may approach 60 in spots
on Wednesday and more firmly into the low to 60s for Thursday. 
The aforementioned short wave will dampen the upper ridge, but 
not to an extent that any notable forcing appears to extend as 
far south as the local area. A dry forecast will be maintained 
through Thursday.

Low level front associated with Great Lakes Thu wave will hang up 
well north of the local area with southerly flow ramping up again 
Friday night into Saturday in advance of more substantial eastern 
Pacific upper level trough. Medium range guidance hints at 
potential of two surges of better moisture advection, one well 
out ahead of the synoptic wave on Saturday evening, and then 
axis of better pooled moisture along accompanying low level 
frontal zone for early Sunday morning. While this short wave 
does not have a full latitude connection to any better northern 
stream phasing, there does appear to be some better dynamics in 
play with this system and decent frontal push which argues for 
maintaining high chance/low likely rain shower PoPs Saturday 
night into Sunday. This does not appear to be a significant 
system in terms of rainfall amounts however, as all forcing 
mechanisms and pockets of deeper moisture will be progressive in
nature. Continued much above normal temperatures will continue 
Friday and Saturday transitioning to slightly below normal early
next week.

Looking ahead, medium range guidance remains consistent in general 
idea that low level baroclinic zone will likely be sprawled 
across the region for the early to middle portions of the next 
week. Consensus idea is for maintenance of active eastern 
Pacific parade of short waves, with some potential of episodes 
of stronger warm/moist advection over this pre-existing 
baroclinic zone. This would likely result in some additional 
rain chances heading into the Day 8 to 10 timeframe.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z WEDNESDAY/...
Issued at 1240 AM EST Tue Nov 17 2026

VFR conditions are expected at the terminals tonight, with light
south-southwesterly flow developing towards morning. Given winds
picking back up, less favorable moisture profiles, and a few
high clouds around suspect that the BR/FZFG potential is lower
despite a few sites around 3-5SM. Left out MVFR potential given
lower confidence for now.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...Air Quality Alert until 10 AM EST this morning for INZ005.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Marsili
AVIATION...MCD

SPC AC 170554

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1154 PM CST Mon Nov 16 2026

   Valid 171200Z - 181200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not forecast in the U.S. today and tonight.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   At mid-levels, a ridge will build northeastward into the Mississippi
   and Great Lakes region today as a trough moves across the Gulf.
   Ahead of the trough, a moist airmass will be in place from near the
   trough eastward across the Florida Peninsula. A large cluster of
   thunderstorms will develop ahead of the trough over the eastern Gulf
   this afternoon. Ahead of this large cluster, isolated storms are
   expected to develop during the mid to late afternoon across parts of
   the western Florida Peninsula. The eastern edge of the large complex
   will likely affect parts of western Florida during the evening.
   Although a strong wind gust or two will be possible, no appreciable
   severe weather threat is forecast.

   In the western U.S., an upper-level trough will approach the West
   Coast today. Ahead of this system, isolated storms will be possible
   along the coasts of northern California and far southwest Oregon.
   Scattered storms will also be possible across parts of the
   Intermountain West. Instability in these two areas is expected to be
   too weak for a severe threat. Elsewhere across the continental U.S.,
   thunderstorms are not forecast today and tonight.

   ..Broyles/Chalmers.. 11/17/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 170659

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1259 AM CST Tue Nov 17 2026

   Valid 181200Z - 191200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are not expected Wednesday.

   ...Central Plains...
   A shortwave trough over the central Rockies is forecast to rapidly
   lift northeastward across the Plains toward the Canadian border
   Wednesday. A surface low will intensify in tandem with the passage
   of the upper wave. Very modest moisture return ahead of a tightening
   surface trough/dryline, coupled with cool mid-level temperatures
   aloft, may support adequate buoyancy for isolated shallow convection
   with perhaps a few lightning strikes across parts of the central
   Plains.

   ...West Coast...
   Along the West Coast, an upper wave will begin moving onshore across
   the OR/CA coasts early Wednesday morning. Cold temperatures aloft
   will likely support isolated to scattered thunderstorms along a
   frontal band and just offshore. At the leading edge of the steeper
   mid-level lapse rates, a plume of higher theta-e air will aid in
   weak destabilization into early Thursday morning. Strongly sheared
   wind profiles may support a few stronger cells. While a sporadic
   wind gust cannot be ruled out, very limited buoyancy inland suggests
   severe potential will be quite sparse.

   ...FL...
   A broad upper low over the eastern Gulf will meander eastward along
   with a surface low. South/southwesterly flow across the keys and
   southern peninsula will allow for inland moisture transport
   sufficient for scattered to widespread showers and thunderstorms
   through the day. Farther north, more easterly flow will support some
   moisture transport/destabilization, but likely much weaker. Overall
   buoyancy appears quite limited owing to poor mid-level lapse rates
   and limited insolation due to cloud cover. Additionally, modest
   mid-level winds through the period will limit deep-layer shear and
   the potential for organized convection.

   ..Lyons.. 11/17/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 170828

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0228 AM CST Tue Nov 17 2026

   Valid 191200Z - 201200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms are possible over portions of California, the Great
   Basin, and into the Southeast.

   ...Synopsis...
   A deep upper low will move inland across central CA Thursday as
   ridging persist over the eastern US. Onshore flow will favor
   thunderstorm potential across CA and parts of the Great Basin ahead
   of the upper low. Additionally, a weak vort max will linger across
   the Gulf producing unsettled weather. Elsewhere, high pressure will
   keep cool, dry and stable conditions in place over much of the
   country.

   ...CA Central Valley...
   Strong ascent beneath the upper-low and an associated 70+ kt jet
   will overspread central CA as a surface low moves onshore early
   Thursday. The low will aid inland transport of Pacific moisture
   which should allow for surface dewpoints to increase from the upper
   40s to low 50s F from the CA coast into the Central Valley. This,
   combined with steeping mid-level lapse rates and cold mid-level
   temperatures (500mb -25 to -30 C) should result in some
   destabilization and thunderstorm potential.

   Model soundings show shallow unstable thermodynamic profiles across
   the Central Valley with elongated hodographs from strong flow aloft.
   This may allow support a few stronger low-topped cells or clusters
   with non-zero severe potential. However, uncertainty on the degree
   of destabilization remains quite high as substantial cloud cover is
   likely. Given the uncertainty, severe probabilities will be withheld
   for this outlook.

   ...Southeast...
   A weak upper-level disturbance will continue to linger over the
   Southeast allowing for another day of scattered showers and
   thunderstorms. Buoyancy and lapse rates will remain modest, which
   should limit overall convective intensity. However, an isolated
   damaging gust cannot be completely ruled out over portions of
   southern GA into the FL Peninsula where scattered thunderstorm
   coverage is expected.

   ..Lyons.. 11/17/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
